exposure: candidate genes (DRD4, DRD2, 5-HTTLPR, COMT, and MAOA)
cohort: 1667 participants from the general population or clinic-referred cohort of the TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey.
finding: The influence of pregnancy and delivery complications on ADHD symptoms decreased over time, while gene-environment interactions (low activity MAOA genotype with low birth weight, 5-HTTLPR LL-allele with pregnancy/delivery complications or maternal smoking) showed stronger associations with ADHD symptoms in early adolescence that decreased over time.
followup_time: 10-18 years old (mean ages of 11.1, 13.4, and 16.2 years)
